title: [SDK 52] expo-location returns denied before the iOS background-location prompt completes
body: On iOS with Expo SDK 52 and the new architecture disabled, I have to call `await Location.requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` twice. After I grant foreground access with “Allow While Using App” and then choose “Change to Always Allow” in the background-permission prompt, the first call reports that permission was not granted. Tapping my button again reports the permission correctly. I can reproduce this in Expo Go, a development build, and a standalone app using the linked Snack.

symptoms_visible: On iOS, after I allow foreground location and choose “Change to Always Allow,” the first background-permission request reports that permission was not granted.
If I run the request a second time, it reports the background permission that I already granted.
N0.label: N0 premature denied result reported

symptoms_visible: After changing the iOS flow to request only background permission, the request can still report “not granted” before I have selected anything in the permission dialog.
N1_x.label: N1_x background-only advice rejected

symptoms_visible: The background request returns “denied” without waiting for my response after foreground permission has already been requested.
The foreground and background requests belong to different feature decisions, so I cannot always request background access when the user first opens the map.
N1.label: N1 valid sequential-permission use case established

symptoms_visible: In the minimal demo, the background permission dialog remains on screen while the awaited request has already returned “denied.”
The app is inactive while the permission dialog is open; after it becomes active again, querying the permission sees the updated choice.
N2.label: N2 permission lifecycle captured

symptoms_visible: With the lifecycle workaround in my production app, the flow waits for the app to become active and then obtains the actual background-permission result.
The underlying Expo request can still return “denied” prematurely without the workaround.
N_terminal.label: terminal application flow works with lifecycle workaround

symptoms_visible: After replacing the background-only attempt with the lifecycle workaround, my production permission flow obtains the updated result when the app becomes active again.
The underlying Expo request can still return “denied” prematurely without the workaround.
N_terminal_x.label: terminal recovery after background-only attempt

solution.intent: Avoid requesting foreground and background location in sequence on iOS; request only background permission because it can request the necessary foreground access automatically.
solution.concrete_example: On iOS, skip `requestForegroundPermissionsAsync()` and call only `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()`.

edges.comment: Comments c4-c10 and c28-c38, reporter's system: the maintainer initially advised requesting only background permission on iOS. The reporter changed the flow and later stated that a background request by itself could still resolve as not granted before any selection, so this did not address the reported asynchronous result bug.

question_patterns: Why does your app need to request foreground and background location separately?
Can you describe when each location permission is requested in the real app?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My map only needs foreground location, while a separate background-check feature needs background access. Most users never use that second feature, so I may request foreground access when they use the map and request background access much later only if they enable background checks. In another affected delivery app, foreground is requested at login and background is requested when the driver goes online.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My app never needs foreground-only access; it can request background location as its first and only location request.
The second feature is enabled after several days rather than several months, but the two permission decisions are still separate.

question_patterns: Did the same permission flow work with an earlier Expo SDK?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The same foreground-then-background flow worked for me with SDK 51 on the old architecture. After upgrading to SDK 52, the background request returns “denied” without waiting for my response.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It behaved this way in SDK 51 too, and I cannot identify any Expo upgrade where it changed.

question_patterns: Can you provide a minimal public repository containing only the permission flow and reproduction instructions?
Please share a standalone minimal example we can run outside Snack.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created a minimal repository with only the permission requests and added reproduction instructions to its README: https://github.com/participant3/expo-location-repro

edges.comment: Comments c9, c12-c21: the original reporter and another affected developer explain why foreground and background requests are legitimately separate and sequential. The SDK 51 comparison and public repository come from participant3; affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you record the minimal example and show the returned statuses relative to the iOS permission dialog?
Please run the foreground-then-background reproduction in one session and report exactly when each promise resolves.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the demo, foreground permission is granted and I then request background permission in the same session. The background dialog appears, but the awaited call returns `denied` while the dialog is still open and before I have answered it. I attached the reproduction material and a recording of that behavior.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The background request stays pending until I answer the dialog and then returns the status matching my selection.
The same early `denied` result occurs, but the foreground permission was granted earlier in the day rather than immediately before the background request.

question_patterns: What application lifecycle state do you observe while the permission dialog is displayed?
Can you log the application state while the permission dialog is open and when the request returns its status?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: While the iOS permission prompt is displayed, my app state is `inactive`. The request has already returned `denied` even though I have not dismissed the prompt.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The app remains active throughout the dialog and never emits an inactive-to-active transition.

question_patterns: After dismissing the permission dialog and returning to the app, what does a fresh permission query report?
Does querying the permission again after the prompt closes return the user's actual selection?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After I answer the prompt and the app becomes active again, `getBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` reports the updated permission. That is also why pressing the original button a second time shows that permission was granted.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A fresh query after returning to the app still reports `denied`, and iOS Settings also shows that background access was not granted.

edges.comment: Comments c30, c37, c40 and c50: affected users provide the raw timing, lifecycle state, recording, and post-prompt query result. Comment c42 is the maintainer's conclusion from this evidence and is intentionally reserved for the consuming solution's engineer inference.

solution.intent: Treat the immediate denied result as a premature SDK response during the iOS permission lifecycle. Until the library is fixed, synchronize the sequential permission flow with the application returning active and obtain a fresh background-permission status instead of trusting the result returned while the prompt is open.
solution.concrete_example: Request foreground access when needed. Before starting a later background request, ensure the app has returned to `active`; if `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` returns while the app is inactive, listen for the next `active` transition and then call `getBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` to obtain the user's actual choice. Remove the lifecycle workaround once Expo ships and verifies a library fix.
solution.inference_hint: From the recording and repository, the maintainer eventually accepted that requesting foreground and then background permission in the same session reproduces a real bug: the background request resolves before the iOS authorization interaction completes. The reporter supplied timing and statuses; classifying that behavior as an Expo regression is the engineer-side conclusion.

edges.comment: Comments c25, c30, c42 and c50: an AppState-based workaround is proposed, the reporter adapts it and confirms it works in production, and another affected developer refines the flow by waiting for active before requesting background access. The maintainer acknowledges the same-session bug and promises a fix, but the thread contains no affected-user confirmation of a shipped package fix; terminal resolution is therefore limited to the verified application workaround.

solution.intent: Recover from the unsuccessful background-only change by handling the premature SDK result around the iOS permission lifecycle: wait for the app to return active and query the background permission again.
solution.concrete_example: Restore the permission flow required by the app. If the background request returns while the iOS dialog has made the app inactive, wait for the next `active` event and call `getBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` before deciding whether access was granted.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut gives the real lifecycle workaround after the reporter has already falsified the background-only advice, without requiring the complete reproduction and maintainer acknowledgment collected on the canonical path.

edges.comment: Recovery edge for the reporter's rejected background-only implementation. It copies the eventual production workaround from c30 so the blind-path aftermath remains solvable, while explicitly marking the diagnostic evidence skipped by this shortcut.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted bug: on iOS with the affected Expo Location flow, requesting foreground and then background permission can cause `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync()` to resolve as denied before the authorization prompt has completed; the immediate value does not necessarily represent the user's choice.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the minimal reproduction and observed timing: the permission dialog remains open, the app is inactive, and a fresh query after the app returns active sees the updated permission.
Must not present requesting only background permission as a complete fix for this case; the reporter implemented that direction and still observed premature not-granted results.
The practical workaround must synchronize with the app returning active and then obtain a fresh background-permission status, rather than trusting a denied result returned while the prompt is open.
Must describe the AppState-based code as a temporary application workaround. The thread does not establish that an Expo package fix shipped or that an affected user verified such a release.
Must ask the user to verify that the final queried status matches the choice made in the iOS prompt before treating the application flow as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Expo/React Native application developer who can build a Snack, share production TypeScript, reason about foreground versus background feature requirements, and implement an AppState-based asynchronous workaround.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and persistent, with imperfect English but clear code examples and concrete product scenarios; challenges explanations that conflict with observed behavior and confirms when a workaround works in production.
